style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: Telephoto 200mm compression photograph in a warehouse aisle: a fleet of identical unbranded autonomous mobile robots massed in receding rows, their safety-yellow polymer shrouds and brushed-steel masts stacked by the long lens into one dense overlapping wave. Hard directional light rakes from the aisle's far end, throwing long shadows across sealed concrete and rim-lighting galvanised racking. Graphite, safety yellow and concrete grey palette, crystal-clear air, deep industrial contrast, no haze. The lead robot sits off-centre on the lower third, compressed rows deepening behind it, generous negative space of dark steel uprights above. Fine film grain, no people, no text, no logos.
rationale: Scale and simultaneity are the story: a fleet that arrives together and returns as one bill. 200mm compression stacks identical robots into a massed wave that no single-object shot could tell, and the warehouse aisle grounds it in the site's world. The treatment also breaks cleanly from the last four illustrations.
cue: The machines arrive together, age together and fail together
subject: A fleet of identical unbranded warehouse mobile robots massed in receding rows
core_thesis: A robot fleet bought in a single year comes back 8.3 years later as one renewal bill roughly eight times the annual charge, and a reserve funded at the original invoice covers only about three quarters of the compounded replacement price — so the second purchase is a capital plan, not a forecast.
core_conflict: The one-year fleet purchase versus the concentrated renewal wave: machines that arrive together age and fail together, while equipment price inflation compounds against reserves funded at the original invoice.
composition: 200mm telephoto compression stacking overlapping rows of identical robots into one massed wave; lead unit off-centre on the lower third, dark racking negative space above
